summary: S. Kuppuswami Sastri was an indologist and philosopher who studied at St. Peter's College, the University of Madras, and under traditional teachers Brahmendra Sarasvati and Nilakanta Sastri. He served as Principal of Madras Sanskrit College and Rajah's College, and later held professorships at Presidency College and Annamalai University.

S. M. Natesa Sastri worked in Indology and other fields, having studied at Government Arts College, Kumbakonam, and the University of Madras. From approximately 1882 to 1884, he served as an assistant to Robert Sewell at the Archaeological Survey of India.

S. N. Balagangadhara is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at National College, Bangalore, and completed his doctorate at Ghent University under Etienne Vermeersch, later serving as a director at Ghent University from around 1991 to 2017.
S. N. Krishna is an Indology scholar attested in 2026 as a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, where he studied under doctoral supervisor T. V. Vasudeva.
S. N. Savadi worked in the field of Indology and held posts at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, attested in 1953 and 1969.
Shrinivas Narayan Tadpatrikar was an Indologist who held positions at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, attested in 1939 and serving as Supervisor of Collations as attested in 1942.

S. Rajavelu is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as an Assistant Superintending Epigraphist at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 2011) and as a Professor in the Department of Marine Archaeology at Tamil University (attested 2015).

S. S. Janaki was an Indologist who studied under Thomas Burrow from around 1968 to 1971. She later served as a supervisor and guide at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute from approximately 1983 to 1999.

S. S. Suryanarayana Sastri was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who worked at the University of Madras, serving as Reader in Indian Philosophy as attested in 1929 and as Reader and Head of the Department of Philosophy as attested in 1942.

S. Sankaranarayanan was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. He served as an honorary professor at the Adyar Library and Research Centre from around 1985 to 1999 and held a post at the Chinmaya International Foundation in 1999.

S. Sankararama Sastri was an Indology scholar who served as a pandit in the publication section of the Oriental Manuscripts Library (attested 1943) and as a pandit at the University of Kerala (attested 1944).

S. Sepideh Hosseini is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. She earned a bachelor's degree at Islamic Azad University, Damavand Branch, and completed an Indian language course at the University of Tehran.

S. Srikanta Sastri was a historian, archaeologist, and Indologist who studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore, and under M. H. Krishna. He held a post at the University of Mysore from around 1926 to 1960.

S. Swaminathan is an archaeologist, historian, and Indologist who studied under J. Sundaram. He worked for the Archaeological Survey of India until retiring as Deputy Superintending Epigraphist by 2013.

Saba Mahmood was a scholar in religious studies and sociocultural anthropology who studied at the University of Washington and Stanford University. She held posts at the University of Chicago (~2000–2004) and as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley (2004–2018).

Sabine Löhr is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Freiburg and the University of Hamburg, completing her doctorate under Lambert Schmithausen. She also served as a student/research assistant (Wissenschaftliche Hilfskraft) at the University of Hamburg.
Sabriye Tenberken is a Tibetologist who studied at the University of Bonn from around 1990 to 1997 and co-founded Braille Without Borders.

Saburō Hasegawa studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1926 to 1929. He later held teaching posts at the American Academy of Asian Studies (~1954–1957) and the California College of the Arts (~1955–1957).
Sachin Kathale is a scholar in computational linguistics and Indology who completed an M.Phil. at Jawaharlal Nehru University by 2007 and has taught at Samskrita Bharati.

Sadajiro Sugiura was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Rikkyo University, the University of Pennsylvania, and the Episcopal Divinity School. He held positions at the University of Pennsylvania, Army War College, and Rikkyo University.
